name: v31-card-visit
description: ⚠️ 10/09/2026, THE NOTICE BOARD VISIT: ONE MORE PASSENGER, AND IT IS THE BOARD'S OWN THRESHOLD. Dean ruled rules.economy.noticeBoardThreshold to 3 for the notice-board-visit arm (S8, docs/notice-board-visit-handoff-2026-09-10-v2.md), where it had been 2 since 20/08/2026, so THE BASE VALUE MOVED UNDER THIS CONTROL. Under 'card' the Notice Board is a BLOCKING building that clogs at its threshold, and 2 is not a detail of that game: it is the brake on the self-visit, it is what shuts a farm to the table in two placements, and every v31 number in reports/ was measured with it. So the `set` below now pins rules.economy.noticeBoardThreshold 2 by name. ⛔ THIS IS THE 05/09/2026 LESSON A THIRD TIME - AN ARM THAT BUNDLES KNOBS RULES IN THE BUNDLE, SO NAME THE PASSENGERS BEFORE RULING, NOT AFTER - and it is the version of that lesson nobody had met yet: not an arm carrying a knob it did not argue for, but a CONTROL silently re-pointed by somebody else's ruling. A control that moves is not a control. ⚠️ AND THE SAME MOVE OPENS A THIRD TEXT DIVERGENCE, on top of the two below: the printed face still says 2 and the base override now says 3, so under the SHIPPED game the card and the rule disagree until Isle-of-Farms-v36.xlsm catches up. Under this arm they agree again, which is the whole point of the pin. ⚠️ THE UI IS NOT COVERED BY IT: packages/ui/src/session/table.ts carries its own inline copy of this pin and that copy does not name the threshold, so the interface silently reads 3 until somebody adds it there too. A copy of a pin stops being a pin the moment the default moves under it. ⚠️ 09/09/2026, THE COMMONS FLIP: THIS ARM NOW PINS THE PASSENGERS AS WELL. Dean ruled the commons in as the engine DEFAULT (docs/commons-handoff-2026-09-09-v1.md), which moved four leaves at once - rules.turn.visitCurrency to 'commons', rules.turn.bonusTiming to 'start', rules.turn.startingMeeplesPerColour to 0, and the Orchard door's printed draw to 2/2. An overlay that pins only what it is named for stops being the arm it is called, silently, which is the 05/09/2026 lesson written down: NAME THE PASSENGERS BEFORE RULING AN ARM IN. So the `set` below carries every leaf this arm's game relied on, whether or not it was in the original experiment. ⚠️ AND ONE THING IT STILL CANNOT PIN: the Orchard door's printed `actionText` now reads "Draw 2.", because that is the shipped rule, and an overlay may never override text. Under this arm the card face and the rule disagree by one card. That is the second documented place where this control is not bit-identical to the game it reproduces (the first is W17 The Pie Shop, below), and both are text rather than rules. ⭐ 05/09/2026: DEAN RULED R17 IN AND THE ENGINE DEFAULTS MOVED WITH IT. The shipped game is now meepleAsCard true, meepleAsCardGoesTo 'board', slotToll 1 and meepleCapPerColour 2, which is exactly overlays/meeple-on-board-v1.overlay.json. ⚠️ SO THIS CONTROL NOW PINS FOUR KNOBS RATHER THAN ONE. visitCurrency 'card' alone would leave the v31 game holding R15's meeple payments, a priced slot and a cap of two, none of which existed in September's game, so meepleAsCard false, slotToll null and meepleCapPerColour 1 are pinned beside it. Without that pinning this arm would silently stop being the v31 game while still being called it. THE CONTROL. This is the v31 game as it stood from 02/09/2026 to 04/09/2026, and it is the arm every future comparison is read against, because on 04/09/2026 Dean ruled the meeple loop in and the shipped default became rules.turn.visitCurrency 'meeple'. The knob did not go away when it stopped being an experiment; it turned around. WHAT THIS OVERLAY PUTS BACK, all of it at once, which is why it is a control and not a proposal. A visit is bought with ONE CARD FROM YOUR HAND, and the card is placed on a Notice Board, so the visitor pays in the same currency they build and grow with. The Notice Board is a BUILDING again: it has a threshold of 2 (rules.economy.noticeBoardThreshold), it clogs, it is cleared by its owner spending a Harvest, and a clogged board shuts that suit's door to the whole table. SELF-VISITING IS LEGAL again (rules.turn.selfVisitAllowed, true in the shipped data and simply ignored under the meeple currency), so a seat may place its bonus card on its own board and take its own suit's action - the solitaire door that risk 2 of the v31 pass armed on purpose. The bonus slot's other half is the STANDALONE FREE DRAW 1 (rules.turn.bonusDraw) rather than Collect, so there is no way for a host to be paid for being visited and no meeple ever moves between players. The turn-start meeple spend comes back with it: meeples are spent one at a time at the START of the turn, each performing its colour's plain action and then LEAVING THE GAME, which is the drain that made two of the five colours dead. The Orchard door is DRAW 3, not Draw 2, because under a card fee a Draw 2 door hands back exactly what the free option gives for nothing - the self-cancellation law, which has no subject once a visit costs no card. The island seeds a meeple on BOTH delivery spaces of every tile (island.meeples.perDeliverySpace) rather than one on the 3 VP space, so the bag is drawn 12 / 18 / 24 deep instead of 6 / 9 / 12. WHAT IT IS FOR. Three things, in the order they will actually be wanted. (1) IT IS THE BASELINE FOR EVERY DELTA. The meeple loop was measured once, on reference-v11 seeds, and that measurement is now history rather than an instrument: the reference has been re-cut as reference-v12 and no reference-v11 number survives the boundary. Anything that wants to say 'the meeple loop bought us X' has to run this arm on reference-v12 seeds beside the default and read the pair. (2) IT IS THE REGRESSION TEST ON A LIVE CODE PATH. The 'card' branch is not dead code - the engine still carries doVisit's card half, the Notice Board's building rules, bonusDraw, the turn-start meeple spend and the threshold clog - and the only thing exercising them at scale is this overlay. A branch nothing runs is a branch that rots. (3) IT IS THE HONEST ANSWER TO 'WERE WE RIGHT?'. The meeple loop was ruled in on a measurement that was not flattering: the hook FELL, 0.41 to 0.37 per player per turn, and the game got 35-43% longer. It was ruled in on the two things that did move - the two dead meeple colours came back to life (Apiary and Dairy take 46% of door uses against 32%) and self-visiting became impossible by construction - and on the judgement that interaction per GAME rose 21% even as interaction per turn fell. That is a defensible call and it is not a settled one, so the game it replaced has to stay one flag away. READ IN THIS ORDER, and read the noise floor line before any of them. (1) THE HOOK, rival visits per player per turn, and the SELF-VISIT LINE beside it - under this overlay self-visits are legal again and took 22.2% of turns the last time anybody measured them, and an assertion that pools them with rival visits will report a healthy hook while the table plays solitaire. (2) THE BONUS MIX, where the solitaire line is the free Draw 1 rather than the empty-board Collect; it took 67.6% of turns under this arm against the default's 54.2%. (3) GAME LENGTH, which is the regression the meeple loop bought its wins with and the one number this arm is expected to win on. (4) THE DOOR MIX, where orange and cream should collapse back to the bottom, because Sow and Build spend cards and a card-fee visit charges the visitor for spending them. (5) The meeple economy, which under this arm is a faucet and a drain rather than a loop and where 'spent versus gained' is a meaningful question again. TWO WARNINGS. This overlay restores the RULES and not the CARD TEXT: W17 The Pie Shop is now keyed on the visited event as the v33 sheet retexts it ('Whenever a neighbour visits you, Draw 1'), so under this arm it pays its owner for a visit landing on their board but no longer for a cross-table sow onto one of their fields. That divergence is deliberate and is the one place where the control is not bit-identical to the game of 03/09/2026. And the bots are the reference-v12 bots throughout: they price a meeple, a Collect and a wild spend, and nothing re-tunes them when this flag flips, so a per-seat number here is the current evaluator's opinion of the old rules rather than the old evaluator's. ⛔ PASSENGERS PINNED 12/09/2026, WHEN DEAN RULED IN THE PLAIN-ACTION BALLOONS AND THE VILLAGE STORE: the shipped defaults moved sixteen leaves at once - a flight now costs ONE barn card, the Aerodrome is in EVERY game, a flight MINTS at the Store, all four balloons pay their colour's plain action, and the six coin leaves are live. This control reproduces a game that predates all of it, so every one of those leaves is pinned here BY NAME at its old value. That is the 05/09/2026 lesson applied before the flip rather than after it: an overlay that should not move with the shipped default has to pin every knob the flip moved, or a control silently stops being a control. ⚠️ 13/09/2026: rules.turn.selfVisitAllowed true and rules.economy.noticeBoardsBySeats.2 1 are pinned here because the shipped defaults flipped when the commons was deleted, so this arm stays the game it was. ⛔ DELIVERY MEEPLE PINNED 14/09/2026: Dean ruled the delivery meeple ON as the shipped default (rules.turn.deliveryMeepleSpace 1, meepleSpendTiming 'afterAction', meepleSpendPerTurn 1, meepleSpendDistinctColours false) together with two new island rules, the space choice (rules.turn.deliverySpaceChoice true: a delivery names either free space) and the closing draw (rules.turn.closingDrawPerCrate 1: filling a tile draws one card per crate). This overlay predates it, so all six leaves are pinned here BY NAME at their pre-ruling values (deliveryMeepleSpace null, meepleSpendTiming 'start', meepleSpendPerTurn null, meepleSpendDistinctColours false, deliverySpaceChoice false, closingDrawPerCrate 0; 'start' and null are the old inert values, not 'none' and 0) and it still replays its own game. Since 16/09/2026 the balloons, the Aerodrome, the Village Store, the closing draw and the wild substitution are deleted from the engine, so this overlay no longer replays the game it was recorded on. Its pins for the balloons and the Aerodrome, the Village Store and the closing draw were removed with them. ⚠️ 16/09/2026, THE TOKEN ISLAND AND THE TURN-ORDER RULINGS: the island is now two tokens per tile (Dean, R3: a first delivery pays both demands and chooses its token, a second pays the last token plus 2 any; Workers sit on the 3 and 4 VP tokens), and the Vegetable and Dairy boards were retexted (R9, R10), so this overlay's pins of rules.turn.deliverySpaceChoice, rules.turn.deliveryMeepleSpace were removed with the delivery spaces. It pins rules.economy.noticeBoardPower.vegetableWildCards 0 and dairyDiscount 0 by name; under visitCurrency 'card' its island meeples now sit on the 3 and 4 VP tokens, and it now starts with seat 0 and gives one more turn each (rules.setup.firstPlayer 'seat0', rules.endGame.endOfGame 'oneMoreTurnEach'). It no longer replays the game it was recorded on, and nothing measured before 16/09/2026 is comparable as a level. ⛔ WHEAT BOARD RETEXT PINNED 19/09/2026: Dean retexted the Wheat Notice Board (sheet v44) to "Harvest one of your buildings, even if it is 1 card short of full", dropped the hand-to-barn rider (wheatBarn 0) and moved the harvest gate from 'loaded' to 'nearFull'. This overlay predates it and V12 The Auction House ("Discard a card from your Barn. Perform the Notice Board action of that crop") reaches the same power as a card effect under ANY visit currency, so both leaves are pinned here BY NAME at their pre-retext values (wheatBarn 1, wheatHarvestGate 'loaded') and it still replays its own game. ⛔ HAND LIMIT PINNED 24/09/2026: the simulator's hand bound moved from 7 to 10 (rules.turn.handLimit is an INSTRUMENT bound, never a table rule, CLAUDE.md 2.3; the move is reasoned in rules.json's meta.notes). This overlay predates that move and replays a game recorded under the bound of 7, so rules.turn.handLimit 7 is pinned here BY NAME and it still replays its own game.
